text:
Your AI agent is about to get hands.

Anthropic just opened a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard, and it is the most underrated thing announced this week.

Here is the plain version. MCP gave agents a common way to reach software. MHS gives them a common way to reach machines. Microscopes. Liquid handlers. Robotic arms. One standardized driver, reachable through MCP, a CLI, or plain code files, and it works with any model.

Why that matters: wiring a single instrument into a lab used to take weeks, sometimes months. Anthropic says hours.

The part you can actually touch this week is smaller and better. Raspberry Pi is rolling MHS support across products after testing a camera driver, and Hugging Face is adding it to LeRobot. A Pi, a camera module, and an afternoon puts you ahead of most people reading the headline.

And the honest limit is in their own writeup. Researchers had to teach Claude that foaming samples were a physical failure, not a software bug. The boundary is still real. It just moved.

Swipe for the five minute version, including the one thing to try.

Save this for your AI stack.

text:
We asked an AI to build the server that publishes us. It did.

Not a demo. The actual thing posting this.

Here is the honest stack, in order.

Copilot CLI runs in the terminal, outside any single chat app, and still reaches every model. That is the unlock. One place to work, no vendor lock on the brain.

From there it used Azure CLI to reach into the cloud directly. It provisioned the box, brought it up, installed Postiz, and handed back the URL. We watched it happen.

Postiz is open source. It holds the Instagram, TikTok and YouTube channels and schedules the batch.

Then n8n, also open source, sits on top watching comments for a keyword and replying with the guide automatically.

Four pieces. Two of them free. None of it magic.

The reason to show you the wiring is simple. People think building with AI means one clever prompt. It means picking a few boring tools and letting the agent connect them while you supervise.

Comment BUILD and I'll send you the workflow map.
